precepts.text: When she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes ye go a whoring.
precepts.point: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood with censers in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth. What do you do in the dark? Your secret sins.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
When Ezekiel dug in the wall, he saw “every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, or Guadalupe on the walls, today. Ezekiel 23 shows what they were putting on the walls: images of the gods of their enemies.

“Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea”. Israel looked at the pictures of her enemies on the wall, dressed up like princes.

“And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” As soon as she saw them, she wanted them. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes you will go a whoring.

So the imagery on the walls of the temple in Ezekiel 8 was not harmless decoration. The images of other nations and their gods drew Israel's eyes, and her eyes drew her heart after them. It is the same today with the images hung on our walls, and it is why the Lord said, I cannot be around you all, and went far off from his sanctuary.

precepts.text: This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
precepts.point: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood with censers in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth. What do you do in the dark? Your secret sins.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.

precepts.text: The women sat weeping for Tammuz at the door of the Lord's house: the mourning that followed the sacrifice of their own babies.
precepts.point: Manasseh made Judah err and do worse than the heathen the Lord had destroyed before them, the nations Joshua and the elders were sent to kill out of the land for the very same works.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh “caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom”. That valley, Gehenna, was where Israel burned its garbage, our refuse; the Muslims call it Gehenna, their hell. Where garbage used to be burned, they burned their children, in honor of Baal.

There was an order to it. In the spring they held orgies in honor of Ashtoreth, the fertility goddess, a black Hamite deity whose star is Venus and whose nose is knocked off the statues. Everyone slept with everyone, and the women got pregnant. Nine months later, in the winter, came the bull god, Baal, the sun god the Egyptians called Apis. The babies were laid on the plates of the brass bull with a fire under it and around it; as they burned they wiggled off into the flame, and drums were beaten to drown out their screams. That is what Manasseh was doing, by the thousands. Carnival babies, Freaknik and the club today are the same worship of that goddess.

Why sacrifice the babies? Ashtoreth gave birth to a baby god, Tammuz, and Tammuz died as an infant. The same way she lost her child, the women had to lose theirs, and the same way she wept for her child, they had to weep for the children they sacrificed on the altar. That is why Jesus is always pictured as a baby with Mary.

Ezekiel saw it: “Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” That is what they had to do once they were in that idolatry: weep for the babies they themselves had sacrificed. And it was worse than what is brought out here.

precepts.text: The prophet dug in the wall and found a hidden door leading to a chamber of secret idolatry.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
“Son of man, dig now in the wall: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door.” The Lord had the prophet dig through a wall, and there was a hidden door leading to a chamber of secret idolatry.

That is what a secret place is: something hidden behind the wall, that has to be dug into to be found. It is the opposite of cherubims graved openly on the walls of the house of the Lord.

precepts.text: The ancients of Israel did their idolatry in the dark chambers of their imagery, saying the Lord seeth them not.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
Behind that hidden door the Lord showed the prophet “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.”

That is the abomination: worshipping images in secret, in the dark, thinking the Lord does not see. It is not the goodly images made openly for the house of the Lord. The ancients of Israel hid their idols in chambers; Solomon graved his cherubims on the walls for everyone to see, and did not bow to them.
